response: Yes, human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) infection has been associated with an increased risk of hypertension. Research suggests that HCMV infection may contribute to the development of hypertension through various mechanisms, including inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and vascular remodeling. However, the exact relationship between HCMV infection and hypertension is still being studied and more research is needed to fully understand the association.
